## Codes left out on purpose
- **Past or family history and admin codes:** 14F1 H/O eczema, 12H1 FH eczema, ^ESCTHI454127 History of eczema, family history of atopy, POEM scores (38Vp etc.) and referral to eczema clinic (8HTu). None of these show the condition is present now.
- **Other types of eczema:** seborrhoeic, contact/irritant/allergic contact, discoid/nummular, varicose/stasis/gravitational, asteatotic, pompholyx/dyshidrotic, hand/foot eczema and napkin dermatitis.
- **Atopic conditions that aren't eczema:** atopic asthma, rhinitis, conjunctivitis, keratoconjunctivitis and cataract, plus "Atopy" (SN533) and "Atopic state".
- **Other look-alike codes:** lichen simplex/neurodermatitis (M1831), other prurigo codes and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (C3912-1).

**Judgement calls you may want to change:**
- I put the M116 diffuse neurodermatitis codes in Tier 1 because ICD-9 classes this condition as atopic dermatitis.
- I also put M111-97 and M111-99 in Tier 1 because they sit inside the atopic dermatitis code group.
- I treated "Allergic eczema/dermatitis" and "Constitutional/Endogenous eczema" as other names for atopic eczema, which is how SNOMED groups them.

Move any of these to Tier 2 if you want a more specific list.

## Codes left out on purpose
- **Past or family history and admin codes:** 14F1 H/O eczema, 12H1 FH eczema, ^ESCTHI454127 History of eczema, family history of atopy, POEM scores (38Vp etc.) and referral to eczema clinic (8HTu). None of these show the condition is present now.
- **Other types of eczema:** seborrhoeic, contact/irritant/allergic contact, discoid/nummular, varicose/stasis/gravitational, asteatotic, pompholyx/dyshidrotic, hand/foot eczema and napkin dermatitis.
- **Atopic conditions that aren't eczema:** atopic asthma, rhinitis, conjunctivitis, keratoconjunctivitis and cataract, plus "Atopy" (SN533) and "Atopic state".
- **Other look-alike codes:** lichen simplex/neurodermatitis (M1831), other prurigo codes and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (C3912-1).

**Judgement calls you may want to change:**
- I put the M116 diffuse neurodermatitis codes in Tier 1 because ICD-9 classes this condition as atopic dermatitis.
- I also put M111-97 and M111-99 in Tier 1 because they sit inside the atopic dermatitis code group.
- I treated "Allergic eczema/dermatitis" and "Constitutional/Endogenous eczema" as other names for atopic eczema, which is how SNOMED groups them.

Move any of these to Tier 2 if you want a more specific list.

## Codes left out on purpose
- **Past or family history and admin codes:** 14F1 H/O eczema, 12H1 FH eczema, ^ESCTHI454127 History of eczema, family history of atopy, POEM scores (38Vp etc.) and referral to eczema clinic (8HTu). None of these show the condition is present now.
- **Other types of eczema:** seborrhoeic, contact/irritant/allergic contact, discoid/nummular, varicose/stasis/gravitational, asteatotic, pompholyx/dyshidrotic, hand/foot eczema and napkin dermatitis.
- **Atopic conditions that aren't eczema:** atopic asthma, rhinitis, conjunctivitis, keratoconjunctivitis and cataract, plus "Atopy" (SN533) and "Atopic state".
- **Other look-alike codes:** lichen simplex/neurodermatitis (M1831), other prurigo codes and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (C3912-1).

**Judgement calls you may want to change:**
- I put the M116 diffuse neurodermatitis codes in Tier 1 because ICD-9 classes this condition as atopic dermatitis.

- I treated "Allergic eczema/dermatitis" and "Constitutional/Endogenous eczema" as other names for atopic eczema, which is how SNOMED groups them.

Move any of these to Tier 2 if you want a more specific list.

Published UK primary care definitions (e.g. Abuabara et al., LSHTM) count these general terms as atopic eczema. ## Codes left out on purpose
- **Other types of eczema:** seborrhoeic (M101-x, M118x), contact or irritant (M12, M12-x, Myu23–27), discoid or nummular (M119, M12z1-1), varicose, gravitational, stasis or venous (G831, M1y2), asteatotic (M11A), pompholyx, dyshidrotic or vesicular (M252x), and nappy rash (M110x).
- **Neurodermatitis (lichen simplex):** M116, M1831.
- **Family history and past history codes:** 12H1, 14F1. Past history doesn't mean the person has eczema now.
- **Admin and score codes:** 8HTu (referral to eczema clinic) and the POEM score codes (38Vp, ^ESCTPO778212, etc.). These can be added if you want to pick up people being treated or monitored for eczema.
- **Hand eczema (M12z3):** this is mostly irritant or contact eczema, so I left it out. It's a borderline call.

If you want a stricter definition, some studies also require two or more eczema treatment prescriptions (emollients or topical steroids) alongside these diagnosis codes.

- **Other types of eczema:** seborrhoeic (M101-x, M118x), contact or irritant (M12, M12-x, Myu23–27), discoid or nummular (M119, M12z1-1), varicose, gravitational, stasis or venous (G831, M1y2), asteatotic (M11A), pompholyx, dyshidrotic or vesicular (M252x), and nappy rash (M110x).
- **Neurodermatitis (lichen simplex):** M116, M1831.
- **Family history and past history codes:** 12H1, 14F1. Past history doesn't mean the person has eczema now.
- **Admin and score codes:** 8HTu (referral to eczema clinic) and the POEM score codes (38Vp, ^ESCTPO778212, etc.). These can be added if you want to pick up people being treated or monitored for eczema.
- **Hand eczema (M12z3):** this is mostly irritant or contact eczema, so I left it out. It's a borderline call.

If you want a stricter definition, some studies also require two or more eczema treatment prescriptions (emollients or topical steroids) alongside these diagnosis codes.

Atopic eczema is often recorded under general terms such as "Eczema" or "Infantile eczema" rather than the specific word "atopic". Published UK primary care definitions (e.g. Abuabara et al., LSHTM) count these general terms as atopic eczema. So I've split the list into two tables: codes that definitely mean atopic eczema, and general eczema codes that you can choose to add.

## Codes left out on purpose
- **Other types of eczema:** seborrhoeic (M101-x, M118x), contact or irritant (M12, M12-x, Myu23–27), discoid or nummular (M119, M12z1-1), varicose, gravitational, stasis or venous (G831, M1y2), asteatotic (M11A), pompholyx, dyshidrotic or vesicular (M252x), and nappy rash (M110x).
- **Neurodermatitis (lichen simplex):** M116, M1831.
- **Family history and past history codes:** 12H1, 14F1. Past history doesn't mean the person has eczema now.
- **Admin and score codes:** 8HTu (referral to eczema clinic) and the POEM score codes (38Vp, ^ESCTPO778212, etc.). These can be added if you want to pick up people being treated or monitored for eczema.
- **Hand eczema (M12z3):** this is mostly irritant or contact eczema, so I left it out. It's a borderline call.

If you want a stricter definition, some studies also require two or more eczema treatment prescriptions (emollients or topical steroids) alongside these diagnosis codes.

### Table 4 – Codes I deliberately left out
- **Other types of eczema:** seborrhoeic (M101, M118), contact or irritant (M12 family, except the general codes above), discoid or nummular (M119), asteatotic (M11A), varicose, stasis or gravitational (G831, M1y2), pompholyx or dyshidrotic (M252), and hand eczema not described as atopic.
- **Nappy rash** (M110 family).
- **Not a current diagnosis:** history and family-history codes (14F1, 12H1, ^ESCTHI454127, ^ESCTFA453087).
- **Process codes:** referrals (8HTu), POEM scores (38Vp etc.) and adverse drug reactions.
- **Other atopic conditions:** atopic asthma, rhinitis and conjunctivitis.
- **Rare genetic syndrome:** Wiskott-Aldrich (C3912-1).

I've built a codelist for atopic eczema from repeated term and code searches of CPRD. It covers the Read v2 atopic dermatitis group (M11), its synonyms and the SNOMED (^ESCT) atopic terms. Some codes are judgement calls, so I've split them into tiers: Table 1 is the core list, Tables 2 and 3 are optional add-ons, and Table 4 lists what I left out and why.

### Table 3 – Optional: general (unspecified) eczema codes
In UK primary care, atopic eczema is often coded as plain "eczema". Many validated CPRD definitions include these codes, sometimes alongside eczema treatment records. Include them for a more sensitive (less specific) definition.

### Table 4 – Codes I deliberately left out
- **Other types of eczema:** seborrhoeic (M101, M118), contact or irritant (M12 family, except the general codes above), discoid or nummular (M119), asteatotic (M11A), varicose, stasis or gravitational (G831, M1y2), pompholyx or dyshidrotic (M252), and hand eczema not described as atopic.
- **Nappy rash** (M110 family).
- **Not a current diagnosis:** history and family-history codes (14F1, 12H1, ^ESCTHI454127, ^ESCTFA453087).
- **Process codes:** referrals (8HTu), POEM scores (38Vp etc.) and adverse drug reactions.
- **Other atopic conditions:** atopic asthma, rhinitis and conjunctivitis.
- **Rare genetic syndrome:** Wiskott-Aldrich (C3912-1).
